name: Brand positioning creation
prompt: Help us create a brand positioning statement and find market gaps.
expected_behavior: Checks for .agents/<productname>/product.md context
Performs deep web research on competitor clustering
Proposes 2-3 potential 'white space' opportunities
Uses Value Proposition Canvas (Jobs-to-be-done, Pains, Gains)
Uses Perceptual Mapping
Formats output using Ries & Trout formula
References brand-positioning-framework.md

name: Value proposition definition
prompt: Write a clear value proposition for our product.
expected_behavior: Maps customer Jobs-to-be-Done, Pains, and Gains first
Aligns pain relievers and gain creators to the offering
Produces a concise, jargon-free public-facing value proposition
Ties the value prop to the deepest researched pain point

name: Perceptual map and white space
prompt: Where is the open space in our market we can own?
expected_behavior: Builds a perceptual map on two meaningful axes
Plots real, researched competitors and their cluster
Identifies defensible white space the product can credibly own
Validates that customers actually want that position

name: Positioning statement (Ries & Trout)
prompt: Give us a one-line positioning statement.
expected_behavior: Uses the For/Who/Is-a/That/Unlike/Our-product formula
Names a specific target, category, and differentiator
Avoids 'better and cheaper' non-positions
Keeps it concise and memorable

name: Repositioning against a competitor
prompt: How do we position against [competitor] who dominates the category?
expected_behavior: Researches the incumbent's positioning and weaknesses
Finds an attribute the incumbent cannot easily claim
Recommends a flanking position rather than a head-on copy
Recommends competitors-research / competitor-gap-finder for depth
